summary.text: A 69-year-old Chinese woman with myocarditis at age 30 and no subsequent cardiac complications presented with a 3-month history of progressive dyspnea, chest tightness, new-onset orthopnea, reduced exercise tolerance and fatigue, with NYHA Class II deterioration over the past month. Symptoms persisted despite symptomatic treatment at a local hospital and necessitated hospitalization for recurrent heart failure with inadequate response to therapy.

On admission vital signs were stable with bilateral basilar rales. The electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm, left axis deviation, low limb lead voltage and ST-T abnormalities; echocardiography and cardiovascular magnetic resonance suggested cardiac amyloidosis. Serum immunofixation and free light chains were abnormal, bone marrow showed 14% plasma cells, and 99mTc-PYP scintigraphy showed Perugini Grade 3 uptake.

Endomyocardial biopsy confirmed myocardial amyloid deposition, mass spectrometry identified transthyretin and light chains, and genetic testing found no pathogenic variants, confirming coexisting wild-type transthyretin and light chain cardiac amyloidosis. She received diuretic, SGLT2 inhibitor, arrhythmia and etiology-specific therapy including tafamidis; ARNI and beta-blocker were stopped for hypotension and daratumumab/dexamethasone was aborted for toxicity.

After 3 months of treatment she discontinued tafamidis and related therapies because of intolerance of adverse effects, chose traditional Chinese medicine and intermittent metoprolol, rejected monitoring, and had sporadic follow-up with persistent exertional dyspnea. NT-pro BNP and troponin I were serially measured during hospitalization, and no objective progression or treatment-response data were obtained afterwards.
